::: {#cor-connected-edges}
#### A connected graph has at least $n - 1$ edges

Let $G = (V, E)$ be a connected (@def-connected) graph with $n$ vertices.
Then $\card{E} \ge n - 1$, and $\card{E} = n - 1$ only if $G$ is a tree (@def-tree).

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

By @thm-spanning-tree, $G$ has a spanning tree $S = (V, E_S)$,
which has $n - 1$ edges by @thm-tree-edges.
Since $E_S \subseteq E$, $\card{E} \ge \card{E_S} = n - 1$.
If $\card{E} = n - 1$, then $E_S$ is a subset of $E$ with as many elements as $E$, so $E_S = E$,
and $G = S$ is a tree.

:::

:::
